chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Qazvan, from Al-Sakoony, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both) who said:

The Prophet of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Two groups from my nation, if they are righteous, my nation becomes righteous; and if they are corrupt, my nation becomes corrupt.' It was said: 'O Prophet of God, who are they?' He said: 'The jurisprudents and the chiefs.'

key_terms.الْفُقَهَاءُ: Jurisprudents or scholars of Islamic law

ai.seo_question: Who are the two groups that determine the moral state of the Muslim nation according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the symbiotic relationship between the scholarly class (Fuqaha) and political leadership (Amara), asserting that their moral integrity is the cornerstone of societal stability. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the continuity of religious authority and governance, where the rectitude of these two pillars directly dictates the spiritual and temporal well-being of the Ummah.
